texts.facts: The appellant / State of Madhya Pradesh through the Collector has filed the present appeal under Section 2(1) of the Madhya Pradesh Uchcha Nyayalaya (Khand Nyay Peeth to Appeal) Adhiniyam, 2005 being aggrieved by the order dated 08.09.2022, whereby the Writ Court has allowed W.P. No.17389 of 2022. 02. The facts of the case reveal that respondent No.1 / writ petitioner is a partnership Firm engaged in the business of sale of petroleum products through an outlet known as 'M/s Laxmi Service Station' situated at A.B. Road, G.P.O. Square, Indore. The writ petitioner has a license issued by Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL) to sell petroleum products. Initially, the said license was given to M/s Standard Vacuum Oil Company. Before commissioning the outlet, No Objection Certificate was issued by the then District Authority under the provisions of the Petroleum Act, 1934 to the erstwhile owner. Thereafter, HPCL took the control of the said outlet and allotted it to respondent No.1. The respondent Firm is continuously operating the retail outlet by virtue of the agreement of the dealership with HPCL. Currently, the lease agreement dated 12.05.2006 is valid for a period of 30 years. 03. On 02.05.2022, an accident of fire took place while unloading the petroleum product at Laxmi Service Station at Indore by the tankers of HPCL. The incident was reported to the HPCL Officials, who conducted the inspection and submitted the report to the head office. The District Food Officer also carried out the inspection and took the samples and nothing wrong was found. 04. The Additional District Magistrate, Indore suo moto took cognizance of the above accident and issued a show-cause notice to the Regional Manager and Assistant Manager (Sales) of HPCL on 03.05.2022 and sought an explanation within three days. The Regional Manager and Assistant Manager (Sales) replied that the erring driver and helper of the tanker truck have been removed from employment and based on the recommendation of the Three Members' Committee, detailed guidelines have been issued to the writ petitioner. 05. The District Magistrate, Indore issued a show-cause notice on 17.05.2022 to the writ petitioner as to why the No Objection Certificate issued under Rule 115(3) of the Petroleum Rules be not recalled. The writ petitioner / Firm submitted a reply explaining the action taken by the writ petitioner against its employees. Vide impugned order dated 14.07.2022 the learned District Magistrate has cancelled the No Objection Certificate in exercise of the power conferred under Rule 150 of the Petroleum Rules, 2002 and further directed the Chief Explosive Controller, Bhopal for initiation of proceedings in relation to cancellation of the license. The District Magistrate has also directed the Commissioner, Municipal Corporation, Indore for taking action with respect to the The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs M/S Laxmi Service Station on 21 September, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84209663/ 2 business license. 06. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid action, the writ petitioner filed a writ petition before the Writ Court challenging the authority of the District Magistrate of taking impugned action under the provisions of the Petroleum Act & Petroleum Rules. The Writ Court has held that in the city of Indore, the Commissioner of Police System has been introduced vide notification dated 09.12.2021 and as per the definition under Rule 2(x) of the Petroleum Rules, 2002, the District Authority means the Commissioner of Police or Deputy Commissioner of Police, therefore, the District Magistrate has no power to cancel the No Objection Certificate under Rule 150 of the Petroleum Rules. The Writ Court has negatived the contention of the Government Advocate that petroleum is not included in the Schedule appended to the notification dated 09.12.2021 issued by the Home Department establishing the Police Commissioner System in the city of Indore. The Writ Court vide order dated 08.09.2022 has allowed the writ petition and [LEAKAGE_MASK] the order cancelling the No Objection Certificate. Hence, the present writ appeal is before this Court.
texts.arguments: Rule 150 of the Petroleum Rules is reproduced below:- "150. Cancellation of no-objection certificate.-- ( 1 ) A no-objection certificate granted under rule 144 shall be liable to be cancelled by the District Authority or the State Government, if the District Authority or the State Government is satisfied, that the licensee has ceased to have any right to use the site for storing petroleum: Provided that before cancelling a no-objection certificate, the licensee shall be given a reasonable opportunity of being heard. (2) A District Authority or a State Government cancelling a no-objection certificate shall record, in writing, the reasons for such cancellation and shall immediately furnish to the licensee and to the licensing authority concerned, copy of the order cancelling the no-objection certificate. [Emphasis Supplied] 12. As per sub rule (1) of Rule 150, a No Objection Certificate granted under Rule 144 in respect of the location of the site shall be liable to be cancelled by the District Authority or by the State Government, if the licensee ceased to have any right to use the site for storing the petroleum.
